title: How Steve Jobs returned to Apple in 1997 and reset it as an entrepreneurial company
summary: Jobs recounts, in a 2003 Stanford talk, how he reluctantly came back to Apple and decided to act as permanent CEO from day one. His August 1997 email shows the first reset: focus on two markets, equity for everyone, shared sacrifice by executives, and consolidated teams.

principles.text: Hire people smart enough to disagree with you at key moments; they can be right when you are wrong.
principles.quote: when you hire the right people, they don’t always listen to you in key moments in time.

principles.text: Be honest with the people who ask for your real view, even when it is risky for you.
principles.quote: this is a director of a company that I started and that I loved for many years—and still do to some extent. And so how can I not tell them the truth?

principles.text: Clarity comes from realizing what you actually care about; passion decides the hard call.
principles.quote: And I realized: You know, I do give a shit about Apple.

principles.text: In a crisis, act as the permanent leader, not a caretaker.
principles.quote: I was just going to act like I was the permanent CEO, because they didn’t need a caretaker.

principles.text: Renewal starts with decisive, focused steps: narrow to a few market segments and a clear product strategy.
principles.quote: a decision to really focus on two market segments (education and creative content)

principles.text: Give everyone a real stake in success, and have leaders go first by giving up their own cash bonuses.
principles.quote: the Executive Team has agreed to forfeit their current and future cash bonus plans in exchange for more stock options.
